mass_kg.source: USGA/R&A Rules of Equipment, Part 4: a ball weighs no more than 1.620 oz (45.93 g)

radius_m.source: USGA/R&A Rules of Equipment, Part 4: a ball is at least 1.680 in (42.67 mm) across

sea_level_density.source: ISO 2533 standard atmosphere at 15 C, 101325 Pa

density_per_5_c_colder.source: ideal gas law at constant pressure: rho ~ 1/T, 5 K in 288 K

lift.form: CL = a S - b S^2 (the textbook start; the game's fit is in assets/play/tuning/ball.json's flight)
lift.source: polynomial fit to Bearman & Harvey (1976), Aeronautical Quarterly 27:112-122, and Smits & Smith (1994), Science and Golf II pp. 340-347, for S below 0.3; the fit is judged by the TrackMan carries (trackman_tour.json), not taken from either paper

drag.form: CD = c + d S, less a drop at high Re
drag.source: as lift; the drag crisis of a dimpled ball lowers CD above Re of about 1.6e5 (Bearman & Harvey 1976)

spin_decay.source: Smits & Smith (1994): spin decays in proportion to w v / r, about 4-7% per second on a drive

drive_carry_per_10_c.source: rule of thumb from launch-monitor fitting (TrackMan, Titleist): about 2 yards of drive carry per 10 F, through the air's density alone

acceptance.note: Fed each TrackMan launch (ball speed, launch, spin) in calm sea-level air, the flight's carry is within carry_share of TrackMan's for 3W-PW, the driver within driver_carry_share: fitted on condition that thin and warm air carry further (the temperature reference, and about 5-8% more carry 1600 m up), the point model leaves the drive about 4% short, which its club spec makes up (docs/plan.md 5.5.3's one named correction).
